title: Android TV: install updates from inside the app
summary: When GitHub has a newer release, the app downloads the APK and starts the Android install itself.

fields.why: The Open button in Settings opens the GitHub page in a browser. Many TVs have no browser, so the user cannot update.
fields.done: On a TV with an older version, one click on Update and the Android confirm screen install the new version.
fields.keep: The update check itself and the webOS and desktop apps.
fields.context: The release check is in AppState.kt (GitHub releases/latest API). The row is in SettingsScreen.kt. The install needs the permission REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES, and the user allows "Install unknown apps" once. The APK must use the same signing key and a higher versionCode.

title: Android TV start waits 6 seconds for a dead server address
summary: The Android TV app opens the home screen as soon as one server address answers, without the 6-second wait for an address that never answers.

fields.why: The user sees the loading spinner for about 20 seconds at each start of 0.2.12 on the Philips TV. About 6 seconds of it is this wait.
fields.done: On the TV (adb 192.168.50.60:5555), the step from the server list to the end of the server check takes less than 1 second, not 6. Measure it on a cold start with log lines or logcat timestamps.
fields.keep: The order of preference stays the same: a direct address wins over the Plex relay. Keep the time limits of each address check.
fields.context: Project rule: every fix goes to all platforms. Check whether the Windows and webOS start code has the same wait.
fields.see: Measured on 2026-11-24 with temporary log lines (since removed): the fast address won after 0.17 s (18:47:20.459), but probe() returned at 18:47:26.314. The same happened in all 4 measured starts.
fields.expect: The start continues right after the first address answers. A normal start is then about 6 seconds shorter (from about 13 s to about 7 s).
